SPECIFICATION FOR 
MODULAR LOWER LIMB ORTHOTIC COMPONENTS 

PART II STIRRUPS, SPLIT 



1. Scope— Dimensional and other requirements of split stirrups for modular lower limb braces. 

2. Typ9s — Four types of split stirrups (according to their lobe configurations) shall be as 
follows: 

a) TypB 1 — Free motion, 

b) Type 2 — Limited motion. 

c) Type 3 - Foot drop, and 

d) Type 4 - Double action. 

2.1 The general configurations of stirrup Icbes for the types given in 2 shall be as indicated 
in Fig. 1. 





TYPE 1 FREE MOTrON 



^YPE 2 LIMITED MOTtOM 





TYPE 3 FOOT DROP TYPE 4 DOUBLE ACTION 

FIG, 1 TYPES OF STIRRUP LOBES 

3. Shape and Dimensions 

3.1 Shape— The typical shape of split stirrup (other than lobe configurations) shall be as given 
in Fig. 2. 

3.2 Overall Dimensions — The overall dimensions of the stirrups shall be as given in Fig. 2. These 
dimensions shall apply to alt types of split stirrups. 

3.3 Dimensions of Lo6es — The general lobe configurations for different types are given in Fig. 1. 
The lobe dimensions of each type shall be subject to performance considerations as given In 3.3.1 
to 3.3.4. The detailed dimensions shall be arrived at depending on their individual designs when 
matched with their ankle joints.

STIRRUP. SPLIT 







3.3.1 Free motion ( Type 1 ) The stirrup shall provide en unrestricted movement of at least 45" 
in bcth Plantar flexion and Oorsi flexion when assembled with the anitte joint unit. 

3.3.2 Limited motion (Type 2) -The stirrup end shall be fmished as shown in Fig. 1. Further 
shaping ( as indicated in dotted lines ) at the time of fitting should provide to 25 in Plantar or 
and Dorsi flexion as required. 

3.3.3 Foot drop ( Type 3 } The Irbe shall be so contoured as to provide the following maximum 
flexion when assembled with Its ankle joints at the time of its manufacture: 



Plantar flexion 
Dorsi flexion 



30** 
15 



Additional flexion of 10*^ either way should be obtainable by further manual finishing at the 
time of fitting. 

3.3.4 Double action ( Type A) -The lobe shall be so contoured as to provide equal Plantar 
flexion and Dorsi flexion of 25" when used with the appropriate ankle joint. 

4. Material MUd steel sheet'Strip, cold rolled annealed Grade of IS : 513-1973 ' Specification for 
cold rolled carbon steel sheets ( second revision ) ' or hot rolled annealed Grade of IS : 1079-1973 
* Specification for hot rolled carbon steel sheet and strip {tiyird revision) '. Finished thickness of 
components shall be not less than 3'0 mm. 

4.1 Alternatively stirrups may be manufactured from stainless steel sheet strip 3*0 mm thick cold 
hot rolled annealea conforming to designation 04Cr1BNi10 or 07Cr18Ni9 of 18:6911-1972 
' Specification for stainless steel plate sheet and strip \ 

5. Workmanship and Finish- -All sharp edges shall be deburred. Stirrups shall be free from 
tool marks, scales, surface flaws and pittings. The stirrups shall be buffed clean and zinc plated to 
Grade I (FeZnS) of IS : 1573-1970 'Specification for electroplated coatings of zinc on iron and 
steel { first revision ) '. 

5.1 Alternatively the stirrups may be plated in nickel-chromium and the plating shall conform to 
Service Grade 2 of IS : 1068- 1988 ' Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium 
on iron and steel ( first revision ) \ Holes rendered undersize in ptatng shall be acceptable and be 
reamed to size at the time o1 fitting If required. In the case of stainless steel stirrups they shall be 
buffed smooth, passivated and polished bright. 

6. Packing and Marking -The stirrups shall be marked with manufacturer's name, initials or his 
recognized trade-mark and with the proper identification of the type, size and material. 

6.1 tSI Certification Marfiing - Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — The stirrups shall be packed in polyethylene bags and ends heat-sealed.
